source_review.notes: Reviewed ten sources covering dependability taxonomy, statistical reliability, repairable and queueing models, dynamic fault trees, fault-tree construction, SRE indicators and budgets, the current ISO product-quality model, cyber resilience, and production failure design. Crossref metadata confirmed the Avižienis et al., Dugan et al., and NIST DOI identities. Official NRC, Google SRE, ISO, NIST, IEEE-linked, publisher, and author records confirmed titles, editions, dates, and scope. The Google SRE page identifies the Implementing SLOs authors as Steven Thurgood and David Ferguson with Alex Hidalgo and Betsy Beyer; ISO identifies ISO/IEC 25010:2023 as edition 2, 2023-11. Mutable pages carry the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed time-to-failure, survival, hazard, point and steady availability, MTTF, MTTR, unavailability, coverage, element reliability, and cut-set definitions.
Confirmed exponential survival, alternating-renewal availability, series, parallel, k-of-n, inclusion-exclusion, and rule-of-three expressions state their domains and assumptions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Mission interval, observation window, binary state, initial state, repair state, and dependence are explicit rather than inferred from notation.

evidence: Recomputed availability 0.998336 and eight-hour exponential reliability 0.449329 for the first example.
Recomputed the 21.6-minute budget, series availability 0.9985005 and 64.78 minutes, conditional parallel 0.9999 and common-dependency result 0.9949005.

Recomputed two-of-three reliability 0.998816, exponential reliability 0.980199, restoration comparisons 0.997230/0.999306/0.998613, OR probability 0.0298, coverage interruption 69 minutes and availability 0.998403, rule-of-three bound 0.01, and exercise series downtime 172.28 minutes.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All decimal results are rounded consistently and retain the model qualifications in the chapter.

evidence: Verified exponential survival integrates a constant hazard and yields MTTF=1/lambda for positive lambda.
Verified the alternating up/down ratio A=MTTF/(MTTF+MTTR) and independent series, parallel, and binomial k-of-n forms.
Verified inclusion-exclusion subtracts event intersection and the common-dependency factor belongs in series with the conditional redundant subsystem.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No expression is extended to dependence, nonstationary hazard, stateful failover, or repair contention without a new model.

evidence: Reviewed frequent brief failure, one long outage, zero observed failures, time versus request indicators, low-volume windows, missing telemetry, and degraded partial service.
Reviewed split brain, stale state, duplicate effects, cold capacity, false detection, failed fencing, simultaneous repair, recurrence, and unavailable operators or tools.
Reviewed common software, configuration, identity, DNS, network, power, provider, supplier, clock, deployment, operator, and recovery authority as dependence cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Catastrophic, unsafe, unlawful, inaccessible, corrupt, or concentrated outcomes cannot be averaged into permission by a remaining error budget.

evidence: Traced fault activation through error state, containment or propagation, service-boundary failure, detection, recovery, validation, and reintegration.
Confirmed reliability, availability, maintainability, durability, safety, integrity, confidentiality, and accessibility remain distinct.
Confirmed every redundancy claim includes detection, isolation, fencing, routing, state, capacity, repair, and common-cause questions.
invariant_checking.notes: Restore means useful validated service, not process restart or endpoint reachability alone.

evidence: Reviewed the series, parallel, k-of-n, OR-gate, repair-availability, and constant-hazard calculations for premise use.
Reviewed the counterexample in which a shared control dependency dominates two nominally redundant replicas.
Reviewed the zero-failure rule of three as an approximate one-sided bound conditional on Bernoulli independence, representativeness, and no censoring.
proof_review.notes: The chapter does not claim statistical, safety, security, regulatory, or production-system proof beyond the declared models.

evidence: Audited uses of reliability, available, independent, guarantee, safe, prove, coverage, zero, expected, and certify for explicit qualifications.
Confirmed probability model, estimator, observed indicator, architecture mechanism, and acceptance decision remain separate.
Confirmed degraded service and durability never become full availability or correctness by label.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter explicitly reserves domain certification and acceptance for authorized specialists and stakeholders.

evidence: Executed snippet availability-composition with the repository verifier under the recorded Python 3 toolchain.
Observed exit status 0, exact stdout for series availability, conditional independent parallel availability, and the 30-day time budget, with empty stderr.
The snippet report records source, command, toolchain, output, expectation, status, and environmental limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution checks fixed arithmetic only and does not establish real component independence, failure distributions, coverage, service indicators, or common-cause completeness.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed service-boundary semantics, fault-error-failure propagation, dependability attributes, indicators, mission and repairable models, composition, common causes, fault trees, state models, coverage, repair, degraded service, durability, budgets, uncertainty, experiments, and governance for conceptual coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed request and time SLI boundaries, correlated regions, shared controls, capacity after loss, failover fencing, state reconciliation, repair contention, cold recovery, telemetry gaps, rare-event estimation, fault injection, safety limits, ownership, and evidence refresh. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate-depth probabilistic and architecture reasoning, eighteen distinct misconceptions, one reproducible code example, ten varied worked examples with explicit conclusions, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar remote-monitoring transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checks, mathematical recomputation, and one local Python execution do not validate a deployed service, failure distribution, independence, failover coverage, safety case, clinical outcome, privacy control, accessibility, regulatory compliance, or universal reliability claim.
